post: Before you click: Which Founder do you think youll get? Put your prediction to the test with BRI's Which Founder Are You? quiz. Discover whose thinking most closely resembles yours, and explore the different perspectives that helped shape self-government. Take the quiz, then tell us in the comments: Who did you get, and did you see it coming?  https://bit.ly/4rkSuBb  #CivicEducation  #AmericanHistory  #FoundingPrinciples

A government strong enough to protect liberty. Limited enough not to threaten it. How could a newly independent nation achieve both? The Articles of Confederation were Americas first answer. Their story is a window into the hard choices of self-government, with real achievements and challenges that put the young republic to the test. Discover why the road to the Constitution was anything but certain. Watch Understanding the Articles of Confederation, part of BRIs Road to the Constitution series:  https://bit.ly/3UVYkNi  #CivicEducation  #AmericanHistory  #Constitution

100,000 secondary teachers. Educators in 91% of U. S. counties. A shared purpose: helping students understand our Founding principles and put citizenship into practice. BRIs Summer 2026 Impact Report shows the work we've done these past few months: - New ways to explore history. The Civics Innovation Lab is testing a Lincoln avatar grounded in scholar-selected sources and an immersive Revolutionary-era print shop. Each pilot starts with teacher and student needs. - Civic learning that starts earlier. BRI Jr. is expanding to help elementary teachers connect history and civics with reading and writing. - Students turning knowledge into service. Medha and Reshma Lalani of Hempfield High School earned the $10,000 MyImpact Challenge National Grand Prize for Tech Buddies, their nonprofit that has helped more than 3,500 older adults build technology skills and confidence. Teachers bring this work into classrooms. Supporters help make it possible. Students carry their learning into their communities. See the people, progress, and possibilities in our Summer 2026 Impact Report:  https://bit.ly/4xvRDyU  #CivicEducation  #StudentLeadership  #EducationPhilanthropy

He helped write the Constitution. Then he helped change it. James Madison initially questioned the need for a bill of rights. Do you know what persuaded him to become its champion? This Constitution Day, explore how the courage to challenge and the humility to reconsider helped strengthen protections for individual liberty. Its a story about the civic virtues that make self-government work. Watch The Debate that Built the Bill of Rights, part of BRIs Constitution Day programming:  https://lnkd.in/e4KUbzTZ  #ConstitutionDay  #CivicEducation  #BillOfRights

Congratulations to BRI's Director of Content and Learning Design, Kerry Flanagan-Owen, for being selected to serve on the NAEP Civics Framework Development Panel! The National Assessment of Education Progress (NAEP), also known as The Nation's Report Card, is the national benchmark for what students know about civics. We're incredibly fortunate to have someone as talented as Kerry representing BRI and helping shape how civics learning is defined and measured. Learn more about Kerry's selection to NAEP, The Nation's Report Card:  https://lnkd.in/eYwvNGhy
